item.title: Introducing WorldVQA
item.guid: title:introducing worldvqa
item.description: A benchmark for evaluating atomic visual world knowledge in Multimodal LLMs. Authors Kimi Team We are releasing WorldVQA , a new benchmark designed to measure the factual correctness of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). While recent models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in visual reasoning and description, measuring their reliability regarding visual world knowledge remains a challenge.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: I Built Local AI Coding Agents on a 4GB GPU. They Could Use Tools, but Could They Actually Code?
item.guid: title:i built local ai coding agents on a 4gb gpu they could use tools but could they actually code
item.description: Testing Gemma 4, Qwen3. 5, and Qwen3 with llama. cpp and OpenCode revealed the gap between successful tool calls and reliable software development. A coding assistant that can read a file, run a command, call an API, and edit source code sounds like a real software developer. But those are capabilities, not outcomes. I wanted to find out how far a coding agent could actually go on an ordinary laptop GPU with just 4 GB of VRAM — and where I would still need a stronger cloud-based assistant.

item.title: Introducing PerceptionBench
item.guid: title:introducing perceptionbench
item.description: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models Authors Kimi Team We are releasing PerceptionBench , a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities— discovered from how today's models fail, not defined in advance. From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.

item.title: Kimi K2.5: Visual Agentic Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k2 5 visual agentic intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K2. 5, the most powerful open-source model to date. Built as a native multimodal model, K2. 5 delivers state-of-the-art coding and vision capabilities and a self-directed agent swarm paradigm.

item.title: The Interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for AI safety. They seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build.
item.guid: title:the interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for ai safety they seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build
item.description: It’s hard to reason about the safety of neural networks without understanding what happens inside them. Our goal is to be able to explain large language models’ behavior, and to use that understanding to identify problems that are hard to see from the outside, such as situations where a model’s stated reasoning differs from what it’s actually doing. Our early work focused on mapping the internal mechanisms of AI models. Today, we increasingly apply our methods to real models to understand how they think and why they behave the way they do. We’ve developed techniques that allow us to understand models’ inner workings in plain language, making it easier to detect unsafe behavior or dishonest reasoning and safeguard against it. item.title: My Hosting Platform Runs on Two SQLite Files. Here's How I Back Them Up and Bring Them Back.
item.guid: title:my hosting platform runs on two sqlite files here s how i back them up and bring them back
item.description: When people hear that the thing running my server keeps all its state in SQLite, they usually ask the same question. Isn't that a toy database? Shouldn't a hosting platform sit on Postgres, with a replica and a team that knows how to fail it over? I went back and forth on this for a while. Where I ended up is that the database itself was never the scary part. The scary part is a question nobody likes to answer about their own setup.

item.guid: title:i wanted a free cloud gpu i ended up with a server that encrypts 6 gb per second
item.description: My hands-on Oracle Cloud Free Tier experiment revealed the surprising potential of ARM processors, hardware AES acceleration, and free cloud infrastructure. I signed up for Oracle Cloud with a fairly specific goal: I wanted access to a GPU without paying for expensive cloud infrastructure. I had been experimenting with CUDA, GPU-accelerated encryption, local language models, and performance benchmarking. Having another cloud machine available for testing seemed like a useful addition to my development environment. Oracle Cloud’s Free Tier looked promising. Some articles described surprisingly capable virtual machines that could run continuously without a monthly bill.

item.title: Making Failure Diagnosis Reliable with Pensive AI
item.guid: title:making failure diagnosis reliable with pensive ai
item.description: By Praneeth Yenugutala , Victor Dusa , Anastasia Samoilova , Megan Ren , Justin Wei , Marcelo Mayworm At Netflix, data and machine learning practitioners run millions of workloads each day across orchestration systems and compute engines such as Titus, Spark, Trino, and Druid. On peak days, roughly 100,000 workloads fail. When workloads fail, the failure itself is only the beginning. Someone still needs to find the useful signal in several logs, decide whether the cause sits in their code or the platform, and determine whether to retry, reconfigure, or escalate. Even a small share of difficult failures can consume engineering time, waste compute, and interrupt critical data pipelines. Our first answer to that problem was Pensive , an auto-diagnosis and remediation system in Netflix’s data platform.

item.title: Why a Tenured Professor Went Back to School for AI (with John Renne)
item.guid: title:why a tenured professor went back to school for ai with john renne
item.description: #realestateai #aipodcast In Episode #1039, Prof. John Renne (Professor of Real Estate and Urban Planning at Tulane University) joins @JonKrohnLearns to describe what happens when a tenured full professor goes back to school for a master’s in AI. John is a world-leading expert on transit-oriented development who spent decades pushing the limits of Excel and SPSS; learning Python and then vibe coding has let him scale that research by orders of magnitude, from 4,500 American train stations to more than 110,000 worldwide. In this episode, he traces how walkable communities went from academic heresy to the most profitable form of real estate development, explains how computer vision can now put a number on how attractive a street is, describes the undergraduate course he and Jon co-teach at Tulane, and makes the case for AI-led oral exams over AI detectors. item.title: How to Protect Your Systems with Throttling & Rate Limiting - 5 Real-World Use Cases
item.guid: title:how to protect your systems with throttling rate limiting 5 real world use cases
item.description: Throttling & Rate Limiting: 5 Real‑World Use Cases TL;DR – Throttling is a defensive technique that controls the flow of requests to a target system, preventing overload, abuse, and costly spikes. By combining slowing down , rejecting , and ignoring strategies, you can protect both public APIs and internal services. Below are five practical scenarios where rate limiting shines, from stopping DoS attacks to rationing expensive third‑party calls. 1. What Is Throttling? Throttling is the process of ensuring that data requests are forwarded to a target system at an acceptable rate .
